# Logical-structure check: the plan has goals and assumptions. An option "questions" the plan
# only if it denies an assumption the plan needs. The assumption list and the mapping from
# each option to the assumptions it negates are my own reading of the passage, not computed
# from the text. The code only checks that the mapping is consistent and that D is the one
# option negating none.

from itertools import product

assumptions = {
    "targets_are_poor":  "the non-returning students are the ones in financial difficulty",
    "students_competent":"students can do the security work",
    "funds_sufficient":  "the office can pay all non-returning students",
    "students_available":"students have no conflict that stops them working",
}

# What each option explicitly negates (as stated in the text)
negates = {
    "A": {"targets_are_poor"},        # not all non-returners are in financial difficulty
    "B": {"students_competent"},      # students hardly competent
    "C": {"funds_sufficient"},        # limited funds vs. many students
    "D": set(),                       # signed up for English classes: "most", classes are part-time,
                                      # nothing says they cannot also work -> no stated conflict
}

names = list(assumptions)

def plan_works(world):
    return all(world[n] for n in names)

# Exhaustive enumeration over all 2^4 worlds
all_worlds = [dict(zip(names, v)) for v in product([True, False], repeat=len(names))]

result = {}
for opt, neg in negates.items():
    # worlds consistent with the option: negated assumptions are False
    consistent = [w for w in all_worlds if all(not w[n] for n in neg)]
    # option undermines the plan if it makes the plan fail in every consistent world
    always_fails = all(not plan_works(w) for w in consistent)
    # option leaves the plan possible if at least one consistent world has it working
    plan_possible = any(plan_works(w) for w in consistent)
    result[opt] = (always_fails, plan_possible)
    print(opt, "negated assumptions:", sorted(neg),
          "| plan fails in all consistent worlds:", always_fails,
          "| plan still possible:", plan_possible)

cannot_question = [o for o, (fails, possible) in result.items() if not fails]
print("Options that cannot question the plan:", cannot_question)

claimed = "D"
if cannot_question == [claimed]:
    print("CHECK PASS: only D leaves the plan fully intact; A, B, C each deny a needed assumption.")
else:
    print("CHECK FAIL: expected only", claimed, "but got", cannot_question)
